samples.summary: New observer on the shared `['me','optional']` query key overrides sheet-view's deliberate 5-minute staleTime
samples.evidence: `sheet-view.tsx:212-216` subscribes to `queryKey: ["me", "optional"]` with `staleTime: 5 * 60 * 1000`, explicitly to avoid re-asking `/auth/me`. `collab-document-provider.tsx:185-192` now adds a second observer on the *same* key with no `staleTime` (so 0) and default `refetchOnWindowFocus`. React Query resolves staleness per observer, so the provider's observer refetches on every mount and every window focus — meaning opening any editor (and every refocus of one) now issues an `/auth/me` request that sheet-view had tuned away, on every user including anonymous share-link visitors, and the feature is dead code in this build (`@yorkie-js/react` is pinned to 0.7.22 in packages/frontend/package.json:66, below `MinClientKeyVersion` 0.7.23). Other consumers of the same key are PublicRoute.tsx:12 and shared-document.tsx:937. Fix belongs on the new query (give it a staleTime matching sheet-view's).

samples.summary: design-sandbox's `@yorkie-js/react` shim records an invariant this change falsifies: `useYorkie` is now called from frontend src
samples.evidence: yorkie-offline.tsx:82-97 states, as the documented basis for what the shim overrides: "A repo-wide grep of every `@yorkie-js/react` import in `packages/frontend/src` turns up exactly four runtime symbols in use ... Nothing in scope calls `useRoot`, `useConnection`, `useRevisions`, `useRemoveDocument`, `useYorkie`, or `useYorkieDoc` — those pass through via `export *` as the REAL implementations, which read a React Context this file's `DocumentProvider` does not populate ... If anything ever calls one, it throws". `packages/frontend/src/components/durable-yorkie-provider.tsx` now imports and calls `useYorkie()` in `LockRefusalWatch`. It is unreachable in the sandbox today (no scene mounts `CollabDocumentProvider`, and `supportsClientKey()` is false at the pinned 0.7.22), so this is a stale recorded contract rather than a live break — but it is the exact tripwire that comment exists to keep accurate, and it becomes a hard mount error if a scene ever reaches the durable branch after the SDK bump.

samples.summary: design-sandbox's `define` block mirrors the frontend's globals but was not given the new `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__`
samples.evidence: packages/design-sandbox/vite.config.ts:187-197 says it "Mirrors `packages/frontend/vite.config.ts`. Scene source IS real app source: it reaches `process.env` shims and `__APP_VERSION__`, and an undefined global is a hard failure rather than a degraded render", and defines `__APP_VERSION__` for exactly that reason. The frontend's vite.config.ts now defines a second such global, `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__`, read by `packages/frontend/src/lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts:supportsClientKey()`, which is reached from `SyncStatusChip` → `site-header.tsx` — a file scenes.config.json:100 lists as a previewable component. The `typeof __YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__ === "string"` guard in yorkie-capabilities.ts keeps this from being a ReferenceError, so the sandbox merely always answers "unsupported"; without that guard it would be the hard failure the config comment describes. The sandbox config is now out of step with the list it claims to mirror.

samples.summary: New modules depend on `@yorkie-js/sdk` APIs that may not exist at the pinned 0.7.22
samples.evidence: The change pins its own capability gate at `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` (yorkie-capabilities.ts) while packages/frontend/package.json:99 pins `@yorkie-js/sdk` to 0.7.22 and :66 pins `@yorkie-js/react` to 0.7.22. The new code and its suites take runtime dependencies on `MemoryDocStore` (wafflebase-doc-store.test.ts), `Document.fromBytes` / `restoreAppendedChanges` / `getPendingChangesAfter` / `getCheckpoint` / `toBytes` (offline-copy.ts, offline-copy.test.ts, offline-copy-recovery.test.ts), `doc.subscribe('local-changes-dropped'|'persist-disabled')` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx) and `ClientOptions.store` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx). I could not verify these against the installed package — node_modules is not present in this checkout — so I am reporting the dependency rather than a confirmed break. If any value export is missing at 0.7.22 the new modules throw at import; if only the `subscribe` event names are missing, the guarded `watch()` swallows it and every durable document silently reports `unreportable`. Confirm by checking the published 0.7.22 `dist/*.d.ts` for `MemoryDocStore`, `restoreAppendedChanges` and `ClientOptions.store`, or bump the pin alongside the gate.

finding.summary: New modules depend on `@yorkie-js/sdk` APIs that may not exist at the pinned 0.7.22
finding.evidence: The change pins its own capability gate at `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` (yorkie-capabilities.ts) while packages/frontend/package.json:99 pins `@yorkie-js/sdk` to 0.7.22 and :66 pins `@yorkie-js/react` to 0.7.22. The new code and its suites take runtime dependencies on `MemoryDocStore` (wafflebase-doc-store.test.ts), `Document.fromBytes` / `restoreAppendedChanges` / `getPendingChangesAfter` / `getCheckpoint` / `toBytes` (offline-copy.ts, offline-copy.test.ts, offline-copy-recovery.test.ts), `doc.subscribe('local-changes-dropped'|'persist-disabled')` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx) and `ClientOptions.store` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx). I could not verify these against the installed package — node_modules is not present in this checkout — so I am reporting the dependency rather than a confirmed break. If any value export is missing at 0.7.22 the new modules throw at import; if only the `subscribe` event names are missing, the guarded `watch()` swallows it and every durable document silently reports `unreportable`. Confirm by checking the published 0.7.22 `dist/*.d.ts` for `MemoryDocStore`, `restoreAppendedChanges` and `ClientOptions.store`, or bump the pin alongside the gate.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise — that the 0.7.23 capability gate implies the new SDK APIs are absent at the 0.7.22 pin — does not hold, and the only harmful consequence it names is unreachable at that pin. yorkie-capabilities.ts:8-24 scopes MinClientKeyVersion to one thing: @yorkie-js/react's `clientKey` prop alias (React strips `key`); docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:15-18,38-43 records ClientOptions.store, Document.toBytes/fromBytes and LocalChangesDropped as 0.7.20 features and the incremental DocStore as the 0.7.22 prerequisite the repo is already on. The predicted failure mode ("every durable document silently reports unreportable") cannot occur: useDurableDocument puts supportsClientKey() first in its eligibility conjunction (use-durable-document.ts:127-132) and CollabDocumentProvider mounts DurableYorkieProvider only when decided.durable (collab-document-provider.tsx:223,283-286,351-354), so at 0.7.22 no durable client is built, no `store` is passed, and DurableLossWatch early-returns for want of context (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:272); the two subscribe() calls at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:309,340 are never reached. The `store`/`clientKey` props go through an explicit cast (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:45-51), so there is no type dependency on ClientOptions.store. Document.fromBytes/restoreAppendedChanges are not import-time bindings — offline-copy.ts:1 imports only `Document`, and the methods are called inside rehydrateArchive (offline-copy.ts:161,213), reached only via offline-runtime.tsx:229-238 for archives that only the gated durable store can create; getPendingChangesAfter/getCheckpoint are typeof-probed with an undefined fallback (offline-copy.ts:83-88). The one ungated reference, MemoryDocStore in a test, is documented as the published 0.7.22 export the contract suite is run against (doc-store-contract.ts:8,16-18), and the pre-existing store already type-imports DocStore/StoredChange/StoredDoc from the same 0.7.22 module (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1), showing that API surface resolves at the current pin. The reviewer states no evidence of absence, and any absence would be a loud tsc/import failure, not a silent bypass.
